task: Implement the canonical Dynamic Production Compiler that deterministically turns a structured Product Owner-approved Page Schema candidate plus proven Genome, Template Type, Constraint Plan and Media Plan inputs into a compiler-proven Factory recipe/program and exact installable package, without generating arbitrary source code or bypassing Page Preset, Page Schema, Builder, Runtime, lineage or anti-clone authorities.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The Factory already has deterministic 14-page scaffold compilation and all upstream semantic authorities are PROVEN, but the active Loot Vault path still hand-authors Factory pageOverrides, shell/global-style adoption and production wiring in the recipe. A real Dynamic Production Compiler is required to compile a structured Visual First candidate through canonical Page Presets and the proven Genome/Constraint/Media chain into one deterministic Factory recipe/program, so future authoring intelligence can emit bounded structured candidates instead of source code.
observableOutcomes: One versioned compiler contract and implementation accepts an explicit Generator Blueprint, structured Page Schema candidate, Genome, bounded Product Owner intent, Media Manifest and internal visual review state.
The compiler recomputes canonical Production Contracts, Constraint Plan and Media Plan before materialization; invalid or stale semantic inputs fail closed.

The compiler derives template identity, demo namespace/fixtures, Global Styles, canonical shell and Blueprint-owned page overrides from the candidate through existing Page Preset authority instead of hand-authored recipe copies.
The compiler emits an immutable deterministic production program with source hashes/identities, selected Page Preset operations and a compiler hash.
The emitted Factory recipe carries compiler provenance; Generator Readiness requires valid compiler provenance when the Blueprint declares the dynamic compiler implementation.
The compiler invokes the existing Factory scaffold; the scaffold remains the sole 14-page materialization authority and Page Schema/Runtime remain unchanged.
The compiled Loot Vault v2 package is exactly equal to the current canonical package while its Factory recipe no longer manually reconstructs shell/global styles/pageOverrides/demo fixtures.
Lineage and catalog-wide anti-clone are evaluated on the compiler output and remain mandatory; the compiler cannot bypass either.
No timestamps, CI run IDs, random UUIDs, source-code generation, HTML/JS generation, direct DB mutation or publish action participate in compiler truth.
unresolvedRisks: Using a candidate package as an unchecked copy source would merely rename pageOverrides and could bypass Genome/Constraint/Media semantics.
Import cycles between compiler, scaffold and Generator Readiness could create runtime initialization failures.
Page Preset replay may alter node identities or metadata and fail exact canonical package equality.
Compiler provenance could be self-asserted by hand-authored recipes unless it is recomputable and Generator Readiness validates it.
Deriving shell/global styles from the wrong candidate page could produce nondeterministic or incomplete output.
A dynamic compiler could accidentally absorb Smart Intent responsibilities and begin inventing composition from free text before that capability is separately proven.

in: Versioned compiler contract/provenance and deterministic hash.
Structured candidate Page Schema package as Visual First implementation input.
Canonical Page Preset-based derivation of Blueprint-owned pages.
Automatic derivation of shell, Global Styles, demo namespace/fixtures and commerce-readiness evidence where deterministic.
Genome / Constraint Plan / Media Plan recomputation and source-chain validation.
Existing Factory scaffold invocation and exact-package proof.
Compiler provenance enforcement in Generator Readiness.
Loot Vault v2 migration from hand-wired Factory recipe materialization to compiler-derived recipe.
Maturity promotion with adversarial executable proof.
out: AI layout generation, embeddings or screenshot-to-layout inference.
Smart Intent or Smart Auto-Fix implementation.
New Page Schema, renderer, runtime, publish path, database mutation or Control Plane gate.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The compiler will become the deterministic bridge from structured Visual First implementation to production Factory output. Highest practical assurance requires canonical source hashes, Page Preset replay, exact package equality, semantic source-chain checks, compiler provenance, anti-clone/lineage enforcement and adversarial rejection of stale/tampered candidates, while leaving intent inference to later VX capabilities.

acceptanceCriteria: A canonical shoporation.template-production-compiler.v1 contract emits an immutable deterministic compiler program and provenance hash from structured production inputs.
Compiler input identity must exactly match Blueprint template identity and the candidate package manifest; cross-template or cross-version candidates block.
The compiler must independently produce valid Constraint Plan and Media Plan results from the Blueprint/Genome/intent/media inputs before generating a Factory recipe.
Every Blueprint-owned page must be materialized from an existing candidate Page Preset; missing, duplicate or non-canonical page coverage blocks.
The compiler derives Global Styles and shell from the structured candidate and cannot accept caller-authored pageOverrides, shell nodes or arbitrary source snippets.
Compiler output recipe records recomputable compiler provenance; a Blueprint declaring dynamic-production-compiler is not Generator Ready without matching provenance.
Factory scaffold output from compiler-derived Loot Vault v2 recipe must deep-equal the current canonical Loot Vault v2 package.
Compiler result exposes the existing Generator Readiness, deterministic Production Lineage and Distinctness results; any invalid result blocks compiler success.
The compiler contains no persistence, publish, tenant, product, order or database mutation code.

FACTORY-DYNAMIC-PRODUCTION-COMPILER becomes PROVEN only after executable adversarial tests, while VX Publish Readiness, Inheritance Intelligence, Visual Diff Intelligence, Smart Intent and Smart Auto-Fix remain their existing non-PROVEN states.
invariants: Page Schema remains the only page document authority.
Factory scaffold remains the only 14-page package materialization authority.
Page Presets are the compiler's page-level reuse authority; no raw component tree code generation is introduced.
Genome owns template identity/visual grammar, Constraint Plan owns bounded semantic constraints and Media Plan owns semantic media requirements.
Compiler provenance is deterministic and excludes timestamps, run IDs, branches, deployment URLs and randomness.
Product Owner visual acceptance remains separate and cannot be synthesized by compiler success.
Compiler output never publishes or mutates tenant/business data.

failureModes: Candidate identity differs from Blueprint but compiler still materializes it.
Candidate has 14 pages but a Blueprint-owned page type is duplicated or missing.
Genome/Constraint/Media source chain is stale but compiler provenance still reports valid.
A caller manually supplies pageOverrides or shell structures and bypasses Page Preset derivation.
Compiler-generated recipe can be hand-forged with arbitrary provenance and Generator Readiness accepts it.
Compiler output is technically valid but anti-clone blocks; compiler still returns success.
Compiler output differs from the canonical candidate package because Page Preset replay rewrites structure unexpectedly.
Compiler success changes because of runtime timestamps or random IDs.
edgeCases: Blueprint owns all 14 pages as Loot Vault does.
A future Blueprint owns only a subset and intentionally inherits remaining pages from the category foundation.
Candidate carries existing templateFactory metadata; compiler/scaffold must canonicalize it without duplicate authority.
Candidate package object keys are inserted in different order but compiler hash/result remain stable.
Media may be technically fulfilled but not Product Owner-ready; compiler truth must not silently convert that into visual approval.
Same candidate compiled twice must yield byte-semantically equal recipe program/package and identical compiler hash.

alternatives.summary: Compile a structured Visual First candidate through canonical Page Presets into a deterministic Factory recipe/program.
alternatives.reason: It removes hand-wired production materialization while preserving Page Schema, Builder, Factory and Visual First authority boundaries.

alternatives.summary: Generate component trees/source directly from Genome and text intent.
alternatives.reason: That would prematurely absorb Smart Intent/AI responsibilities and bypass existing preset/Builder safeguards.

alternatives.summary: Call the existing scaffold around the existing hand-authored recipe and label the wrapper a compiler.
alternatives.reason: It would not remove manual pageOverrides/shell/global-style production wiring and would be a false capability promotion.

specialistReviews.finding: The existing hierarchy already defines Template → Page Presets → Section Presets → Components; compiler output must materialize through that hierarchy and the Factory scaffold.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use structured candidate Page Presets as the page-level compiler input and preserve scaffold as package authority.

specialistReviews.finding: A provenance field supplied by the recipe itself is forgeable unless its hash is recomputed from Blueprint, candidate and semantic plan sources.
specialistReviews.resolution: Compiler provenance contains canonical source identities/hashes and Generator Readiness recomputes/validates the contract rather than trusting a boolean.

specialistReviews.finding: Compiler success cannot mean the design was aesthetically approved or that it may skip Visual First.
specialistReviews.resolution: Candidate is an already structured Visual First implementation bound to accepted Visual Authority; Product Owner review remains a separate explicit input/state.

specialistReviews.finding: A compiler must not create a second renderer or mutate persisted storefront/business state.
specialistReviews.resolution: Implementation is a pure in-memory derivation plus existing scaffold call; tests forbid persistence/publish/server imports.

challenge.scenario: Candidate package is for gaming.playroom but Blueprint is gaming.loot-vault.
challenge.finding: Cross-template candidate reuse could produce a valid-looking but wrong package.
challenge.resolution: Compiler rejects candidate manifest identity before any recipe/program materialization.

challenge.scenario: Candidate has all 14 pages but two have the same pageType and one required owned page type is absent.
challenge.resolution: Compiler enforces canonical unique pageType coverage and exact Blueprint-owned Page Preset resolution.

challenge.scenario: Genome changes after a previously generated compiler program.
challenge.finding: Stale program could replay against a new template identity.
challenge.resolution: Compiler program binds Genome hash, Constraint Plan hash and Media Plan hash; Generator Readiness rejects mismatched provenance.

challenge.scenario: Media manifest semantic bindings no longer satisfy Constraint Plan.
challenge.finding: Compiler could materialize visually but violate semantic media requirements.
challenge.resolution: Media Planner must be valid before compiler program creation and its hash is embedded in provenance.

challenge.scenario: Caller attempts to pass arbitrary pageOverrides or shell nodes into compiler input.
challenge.resolution: Compiler input contract exposes only structured candidate package and semantic inputs; recipe internals are output-only.

challenge.scenario: Compiler output is a repaint clone of another catalog template.
challenge.finding: Technically valid materialization must not bypass distinctness.
challenge.resolution: Compiler success requires the existing Generator Readiness distinctness result to be valid.

challenge.scenario: Two equivalent candidate objects have different object-key insertion order.
challenge.finding: Naive serialization could create unstable compiler identity.
challenge.resolution: Compiler uses recursive canonical serialization for program/provenance hash and Page Preset selection is canonical-order.

challenge.scenario: Compiler is called twice with identical inputs.
challenge.finding: Random node IDs or timestamps would break deterministic production.
challenge.resolution: No random/time input is permitted; Page Preset materialization preserves stable source identities and both program hash and package output must repeat exactly.

proofPlan: Canonical Loot Vault v2 compiler proof derives recipe/program from structured candidate and deep-equals the current canonical 14-page package.
Static-recipe removal proof confirms Loot Vault Factory recipe no longer manually declares pageOverrides, shell nodes, Global Styles or demo fixtures.
Determinism proof recompiles identical input twice with identical compiler hash, recipe projection and package.
Identity-drift proof rejects foreign template/version candidate.
Page-matrix proof rejects missing/duplicate Blueprint-owned Page Presets.
Semantic-source proof rejects invalid Genome/Constraint/Media chain before Factory materialization.
Forged/stale compiler provenance proof makes Generator Readiness fail closed.
Anti-clone and Production Lineage combination proof remains mandatory on compiler output.
Maturity proof promotes only Dynamic Production Compiler; remaining VX blockers stay non-PROVEN.
Normal CI + exact-head Template Factory Quality Gate v2 + Completion Truth + lifecycle closure.

requirements.requirement: Canonical deterministic compiler derives Factory production recipe/program from structured Visual First candidate plus proven semantic inputs through Page Preset and scaffold authorities, with exact package reproducibility.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Compiler cannot create source/render/runtime/page authorities outside canonical Page Presets, Page Schema and Factory scaffold.

requirements.requirement: Identity drift, invalid semantic source chain, incomplete Page Preset coverage, forged provenance, invalid lineage or anti-clone block cannot produce compiler success or Generator Ready status.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Partial, stale or hand-forged compiler evidence cannot count as valid production compilation.

requirements.requirement: Dynamic compiler completion does not promote Publish Readiness, Inheritance Intelligence, Visual Diff Intelligence, Smart Intent or Smart Auto-Fix.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Compiler completion cannot imply remaining VX intelligence capabilities are proven.
